profile.campus: Goodyear, Maricopa County, Arizona (Microsoft Azure data center campus, part of the West US 3 region)
profile.address: 14250 West Broadway Road, Goodyear, Maricopa County, Arizona, 85338
profile.reading: This building is part of Microsoft's Goodyear, Maricopa County, Arizona data center campus, one of three "world-class" campuses (alongside sites in El Mirage) that Governor Doug Ducey and Microsoft announced together on July 31, 2019, representing a combined investment of hundreds of millions of dollars. Microsoft said the campuses would create more than 100 permanent jobs for mechanical engineers, electrical engineers, and data center technicians, plus more than 1,000 temporary construction jobs, and projected roughly $20 million a year in economic impact for the surrounding Arizona communities once operational. The Goodyear campus runs on 100% renewable energy sourced in part from First Solar's 150-megawatt Sun Streams 2 photovoltaic plant, and Microsoft designed the facility for water efficiency such that it uses zero water for much of the year, pursuing LEED Gold certification with a goal of diverting at least 90% of construction waste from landfills. Microsoft has continued expanding the site well past the original 2019 announcement: Data Center Dynamics reported in June 2026 that Microsoft paid $131 million for an additional 100 acres adjacent to its existing 150-acre Goodyear campus, purchased from Chicago-based First Industrial Realty Trust near Citrus and Indian School roads, bringing Microsoft's total Goodyear-area footprint to more than 550 acres; CoStar data cited in that report counted six data center buildings on the campus either existing, under construction, or proposed. The expansion supports Microsoft's West US 3 Azure region, based in Phoenix. Microsoft has separately committed more than $800,000 to Arizona community development and water conservation projects supporting Lake Mead sustainability. Microsoft has not published which of the six campus buildings this specific OSM-mapped structure corresponds to, nor its individual square footage or MW capacity.

reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or specific technical specifications for individual Azure data center campuses. This facility, PHX-14 in Goodyear, is part of a larger Microsoft campus in the Phoenix metropolitan area and appears on public records as an owned asset, but its contribution to the campus total remains undisclosed.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 operators have published power figures to this registry. Those four facilities total 512 MW, and this campus ranks fifth in the state by published capacity, meaning it is either larger than the published facilities or is being counted in aggregate with other Microsoft properties. Without disclosed specifications, the facility's role in Microsoft's Arizona footprint cannot be quantified.

The lack of individual campus disclosures from mega-operators like Microsoft is the binding research constraint here, not the physical site. This campus matters to AI scaling only to the degree that Azure's global aggregate statistics (40+ GW of renewable energy contracted, 500+ facilities worldwide) reveal Microsoft's overall infrastructure strategy, since campus-level data for proprietary planning facilities remains private.
